rows.note: Use this for something visibly covered in fresh blood, such as a bloody wound or stump.

example.english: That wound is still bloody; it hurts just looking at it.
example.traditional: 嗰個傷口仲血淋淋，睇見都痛。
example.jyutping: go2 go3 soeng1 hau2 zung6 hyut3 lam4 lam4 tai2 gin3 dou1 tung3

rows.note: Use this for violence, battles, or events characterised by bloodshed rather than for something physically covered in blood.

example.english: The war scenes in this film are very bloody.
example.traditional: 呢套戲嘅戰爭場面好血腥。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 ge3 zin3 zang1 coeng4 min6 hou2 hyut3 seng1

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken intensifier before an adjective or adverb, especially when expressing strong annoyance or emphasis.

example.english: This computer is bloody slow; I really can't stand it.
example.traditional: 呢部電腦鬼咁慢，真係頂唔順。
example.jyutping: nei1 bou6 din6 nou5 gwai2 gam3 maan6 zan1 hai6 ding2 m4 seon6

rows.note: Use this for emphatic or incredulous force when the English expletive does not need to sound vulgar.

example.jyutping: zan1 hai6 gam3 dou1 dak1 gaa3

rows.note: Use this before an adjective or adverb for a strongly vulgar ‘so bloody ...’ emphasis.

example.english: Why are you guys so bloody slow at working—when will we finish?
example.traditional: 你哋做嘢咁撚慢，幾時先收工呀？
example.jyutping: nei5 dei6 zou6 je5 gam2 lan2 maan6 gei2 si4 sin1 sau1 gung1 aa3
